<|channel|>analysis<|message|>We need to decide if text is human or AI. The text seems somewhat mechanical, but has some errors: "hitscan has been described so I will cover the other thing . In raycasting a bullet will be generated either as a full model with textures or just a point with an effect . This will be given an initial position of the barrel of the shooter 's gun and a velocity equal to the muzzle velocity . Since the game works in time steps , the bullet will travel for one frame using equations based on its initial velocity and a constant acceleration ( which may be zero for simple engines ) to find its new position , then a hitscan is performed from the bullets previous position to its new position to determine if it hit anything . The velocity of the bullet is to account for velocity changes from that acceleration and then that all happens again the next frame . The hitscan is necessary over just checking each frame if I 'm the collision boxes intersect because if the game engine runs at 60 Hz , a bullet travelling at 300 m/s ( which is slow for a modern bullet ) will travel 5 m in a frame . This is several times the size of a human object 's hit box so the chances that the bullet and target hit boxes actually intersect during any one frame is small ."
